$meta.name: NEMESIS design tokens
$meta.governs: §E6 the press · §E9 colour · §E10 typography · §E11 motion · §E19 density
$meta.rule: This file is the single source. `npm run tokens` generates the CSS custom properties the 2D layer uses and the TSL constants the shader layer uses, from these values, and nothing else may declare a colour — scripts/check-guards.ts fails the build on a literal anywhere else in src/. §E9.4 rule 3: the severity ink in a badge and the glaze in a shader are literally the same number.

paper.$note: Ground. Carries no meaning — §E9.1. Riso ink is translucent and sits on paper, so these are stocks, not backgrounds.

mitti-950.note: the workbench at night — console ground

bone-200.note: body text on dark — never pure white

ink.$note: Published risograph ink colours approximated to sRGB — §E9. The palette holds together because a manufacturer mixed it for overprinting, not because we picked it for a screen.

riso-black.note: base ink — all text, all rules

riso-brown.note: the clay ink — MITTI's body colour

riso-aqua.note: SIGNAL — links, focus rings, primary action, selection

riso-flu-pink.note: FLUORESCENT — flagged / unverified ONLY, always hatched (ADR-0039)

severity.$note:
Fired glazes, printed as inks — §E9.4. Four channels per level and they are not interchangeable: `ink` sets type, `tint` fills a field, `glaze` feeds the TSL severity ramp, `inkPass` names the press separation. `shape` is here because colour is never the only channel (rule 2) — grayscale printouts work, and §E19.7 establishes that officers print.

**The label is deliberately not here.** §E9.4's table lists one, and a first pass carried it across. But a label is copy, not a design token: a token file cannot be translated by the Phase 5 locale registry, so a severity labelled from here is a severity that reads 'Critical' on a Marathi console forever — and Phase 18's gate is that a locale added in the control plane appears with no code change. Labels live in src/i18n/base/common.json under `severity.*`. Colour and shape are design; words are content; keeping both here would have been two sources for one string.

role.$note: Semantic roles, and the answer to a defect this palette had. §E22 sets WCAG 2.2 AA as a floor and requires every pair tested on BOTH grounds. Measured, three of §E9's own role labels did not clear it: riso-aqua as SIGNAL is 2.51:1 on paper-50, mitti-500 as "secondary text on light" is 3.80:1, and severity ink sits below 4.5:1 on kraft-200. Darkening the published Riso inks was refused — they are the premise of the direction (§E4). Instead the fix is the press's own mechanic: §E6.3 says two inks overlapping create a third colour by multiply, so the text-safe value of an ink is that ink OVERPRINTED with a second pass. Nothing is invented, the derivation is computed by the generator, and the result is a colour a real two-ink press would actually produce.

text-secondary.note: mitti-500 alone is 3.80:1 on paper-50 — a second pass of mitti-300 carries it to 6.54:1

text-signal.note: SIGNAL on light. Aqua alone is 2.51:1; overprinted with the cool pass it is 10.60:1, and it is still visibly the aqua ink

rule.note: Was mitti-300, which measures 1.36:1 on kraft-200 — a hairline nobody can see on the zebra stock, which is a design defect even though WCAG asks nothing of a decorative rule. mitti-500 holds 2.79:1 at worst. mitti-300 keeps its other job: disabled.

flag-hatch.note: the 45° hatch itself (ADR-0039). Never carries the text

flag-text.note: a flag's words are black on the hatch, never pink on a ground

text-signal.note: on the light table the raw ink is correct and passes at 6.38:1 — a backlit print glows, which is exactly why §E9.3 refuses an inverted palette

outdoor.$note: §E21's outdoor mode, and §E25 Phase 22's own gate line: "outdoor mode passes contrast at 7:1 for primary text". Near-monochrome with heavier weights and larger type — "design for gloves and glare, not for a design review". Every floor here is 7 rather than 4.5, which is WCAG 2.2 AAA for body text; sunlight on a phone at noon defeats a palette that only clears AA. The stock is `chalk`, the brightest sheet in §E9.1, because on a screen fighting the sun the ground has to be the strongest thing in the frame. Nothing new is invented: every value is an ink §E9.2 already publishes, or two of them overprinted (§E6.3).

text-primary.note: 17.48:1 on chalk. The Phase 22 gate's own clause.

text-secondary.note: A second impression of the same ink — a real press move, and the cheapest way to reach 10.79:1 without leaving the palette. mitti-500 × mitti-300 reaches only 7.18:1 and leaves no margin.

text-signal.note: 11.65:1. The same derivation the light ground uses, so SIGNAL is recognisably the same ink outdoors — near-monochrome, not monochrome: one thing on the screen is allowed to be a colour, and it is the thing you tap.

rule.note: 4.17:1. A rule is not text and WCAG asks 3:1 of a boundary; in glare a hairline below that is a rule nobody can see.

flag-hatch.note: The 45° hatch itself (ADR-0039), unchanged: it never carries the words.

flag-text.note: A flag's words are black on the hatch, at the outdoor floor like every other word.

severity.$note:
Which of §E9.4's four channels carries type, which fills the field, and which draws the mark, per ground. On paper: ink on tint — 5.31:1 at worst.

On the light table an earlier pass filled the badge with the glaze and set the tint on it. That measures 2.63-4.37:1 and axe caught it across all twelve matrix combinations. It was also the wrong *picture*: a solid coloured chip is the inverted palette §E9.3 explicitly refuses. §E9.3 says the prints are backlit and 'the page ground is mitti-950 because that is the room, not the paper' - so the ink glows and the room stays behind it. Tint on the room measures 13.48-15.04:1, and the glaze draws the mark and a printed edge at 3.09-5.72:1, clearing WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for a meaningful graphic. The physics and the floor agree again.

Severity type never sits directly on a table stock; that is what the tint channel is for, and it is why kraft-200's 4.17:1 is a misuse rather than a defect.

role.$floors: Text roles carry the WCAG 2.2 AA floor of 4.5:1. Rules and hatches carry a floor this project set for itself, because WCAG requires nothing of a decorative hairline and an invisible rule is still a defect — §E22's "audited rather than only scanned" cuts both ways.

inkSet.$note: Risograph's real constraint is two or three inks per run — §E9.2. Honouring it is what makes each surface look deliberately designed rather than arbitrarily coloured. `severity` as a member means the third pass is whichever severity ink the entity carries. `gradeGamma` is the run's exposure, applied to the photograph about the sheet's white point before the plates are solved — a printer choosing an exposure for a run, which is a real thing printers do (ADR-0061). It defaults to 1.0, the identity, and only the story run states one. `stock` is the page ground and `sheet` is what the press prints on. They are the same on every surface but one, and the exception is §E9.3's light table: there the ground is mitti-950 because that is the room, not the paper, and the prints on it are backlit. A 3D press given the room as its sheet multiplies ink onto near-black and produces a black frame — which is what the first golden image of the clay actually showed. `sheet` is omitted wherever the two agree, and the generator fills it in.

story.gradeNote: The exposure this run is printed at — ADR-0061, and the open decision in docs/reports/story-press-flat.md. §E9.2 gives the film brown + sunflower + aqua and no black plate, so one plate carries the entire model and the clay body IS that plate's ink (§E7.1). Ungraded, the clay solved at 0.55 lit / 0.91 body / 1.27 shadow: everything from the body tone down printed at or past full coverage, and the landing showed a flat brown field with no city in it. A gamma about the sheet's own white point is one number and it is the whole fix — 0.72 gives 0.40 / 0.66 / 0.89, the same shape a black-plate run has for free (`public` reads 0.27 / 0.44 / 0.58), with nothing clamped until true black, where a solid is what a print is supposed to do. Every other run omits this and is generated at exactly 1.0, which is the identity: no other surface's separation moves by a single bit.

console-night.note: the light table (§E9.3) — the same prints, backlit on glass. Not an inverted palette; inverting would break the premise the direction rests on. `sheet` is bone-200 rather than the room: a backlit print is light coming *through* ink, so what the press multiplies onto is the illumination, and the room is what surrounds the print.

press.$note: §E6. Six stages in order, and the quality dial in §E6.4 is the fallback ladder's first move — the one degradation in this product that improves the picture.

screenAngles.note: classic screen angles, so the rosette reads as real print (§E6.1 stage 2)

halftone.note: round dot, slightly soft edge. Cell size in device-independent pixels.

misregistration.note: §E6.1 stage 3 — the majority of "why does this look printed"

inkDensity.note: risograph ink is famously uneven, roller-streaked, denser at the leading edge of a pass

motion.$note: §E11. A stop-motion world has its own physics. No spring overshoot anywhere in the console — overshoot reads as toy, and this is a tool people are audited on. Durations are multiples of the 12 fps step (83.3 ms), so the whole product beats to the same clock as the animation.

step.note: one frame at 12 fps — the unit every duration is a multiple of

clay.note: heavy objects: slow in, fast out

reducedMotion.note: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all five signature motions to opacity at one step, and switches the landing to the storyboard edit (§E13 Tier C)

sound.$note: §E12. Every number the sound layer uses, in one place for the same reason every colour is — a gain re-typed in a component is a second sound design. Durations are multiples of the 12 fps step (83.3 ms) wherever a sound accompanies a motion, because §E11's whole argument is that the product beats to one clock, and a thud that lands 40 ms after the stamp it belongs to reads as a fault rather than as a decision. ADR-0050: none of this is a file; the generator in src/sound/synth.ts renders these into buffers at runtime.

type.$note: §E10. Six faces, six jobs, all self-hosted — no CDN, satisfying §6 Principle #6 at the type layer. Devanagari is a design partner, not a fallback (§E10.1).

narrative.role: Narrative display — landing prose, report covers

institutional.role: Institutional display — the municipal signage voice

document.role: Stamps, receipts, RTI drafts, case files, report footers

hand.role: The human hand — paper flags, margin notes. One face across Latin and Devanagari

deva-display.role: Devanagari display. §E10.1 named Kaana; it is not obtainable under a free commercial licence, so Sarpanch takes the role — ITF, OFL, squared and straight-lined and wide, which is what §E10.1 described.

scale.$note: §E10.2. The scale is defined per script and is never globally scaled from the Latin values (§E10.1). Devanagari line-height carries +0.15 over the Latin value, applied here by the generator rather than by a stylesheet override.

poster.$note: The floor is 2.5rem and it is Panchang's width that sets it. The step is worn by exactly one element — the film's masthead — and Panchang sets NEMESIS at 6.98em of advance, which is more than twice what the condensed fallback the floor was first chosen against needed. At a 4rem floor the name measured 296px inside a 288px frame on a 320px screen and broke mid-word; 2.5rem clears every width from 320 up with the 12vw term still doing the work everywhere above 367px. Nothing about the poster's presence changes — it is the same size on every screen wide enough to have a choice.

devanagari.$note:
Devanagari sits taller and the shirorekha needs air. `data` and `document` do not remap: an id, a hash and a coordinate are the same glyphs in every locale.

§E10.1 specifies the leading rule as a flat +0.15 over the Latin value. Measured across the whole scale, that is not enough wherever the Latin leading is set below 1.0: Devanagari ink runs to 1.289em at `display-2` and 1.286em at `doc`, against a Latin display leading of 0.94–1.04. The rule is therefore a delta AND a floor — leading = max(latin + 0.15, 1.35) — where 1.35 is the measured ink ceiling plus clearance, not a guess. The consequence is real and correct: Devanagari display type is LOOSER than Latin display type, because the script stacks matras above the shirorekha and below the baseline. You cannot set Devanagari at 0.86. That is precisely what §E10.1 meant by defining the scale per script rather than scaling one from the other. Measured by tests/type.spec.ts, which fails if the floor drops.

numeric.note: Every number, everywhere. A column of costs that does not align is a column nobody trusts, and this product's whole proposition is trust in columns of costs. §E10.2 writes this as `tabular-lining`, which is not a CSS value and computes to `normal` — so the rule was, as written, silently doing nothing. The two real keywords are `lining-nums` and `tabular-nums`. Caught by tests/type.spec.ts.

density.$note: §E19 — three modes, persisted per user. The console is dense because an officer works in it for nine hours.

layer.$note: Compositing order. `text` sits above `press` and is never processed by it — ADR-0038, §E6.2. The value of this token is the reason the byte-identity test can exist at all.

clay.$note: §E7.1's material recipe, as numbers. No colour is authored here: the clay body IS ink.riso-brown — §E9.2 calls it "the clay ink, MITTI's body colour" — and the rim's warm and cool terms are the sunflower and the federal blue. A clay swatch of its own would be a fourth palette nobody asked for, and would break §E5's claim that one press runs over all three materials.

body.note: matte albedo — the clay ink itself

warm.note: the lit side of the sub-surface rim

cool.note: the shadow side of the same rim

surface.note: §E7.1 exactly. Zero metalness is not a rounded-down small number: clay is a dielectric, and a metallic term would put a coloured specular on a material that has none.

thumbprint.note: one tiling normal at low amplitude, rotated per instance by a hash of the entity id so nothing tiles visibly. Sixteen rotations is enough that a repeat is not findable by eye and few enough that the hash stays a cheap integer fold.

ao.note: baked into vertex colours, never sampled. `floor` is how dark a fully occluded crease is allowed to get — clay in a crease is darker clay, not black.

rim.note: the sub-surface cheat. One Fresnel term, warm on the light side and cool in shadow — §E7.1: "this single term carries most of the read".

edge.note: cut-card edges. A thin darker band along the top rim of every extruded footprint, in world metres rather than pixels, so a building does not gain a thicker edge as the camera pulls in.

glaze.note: §E7.1's fired glaze. Severity arrives as a specular coat with a darker rim over the clay body — never as emissive. Emissive severity would make the map glow, and §E7.3 reserves the only glow in this product for safety_trigger_fired.

lens.$note: §E7.3, applied before the press. Everything here is a property of the camera looking at the table, which is why none of it belongs in `press`: the lens is what we photograph the model with, the press is what we print the photograph on.

tiltShift.note: the single most important effect — it is what makes a city read as a miniature. `focusMetres` is an offset from the selected entity's depth, so the focal plane follows the selection rather than sitting at a fixed distance.

gateWeave.note: ±0.4 px, resampled on the same 12 Hz stepped clock as everything else that steps. Not consciously perceptible; makes the frame feel projected.

vignette.note: we are looking through a macro lens at a table.

barrel.note: slight, and deliberately below the threshold where a straight road looks bent.

bloom.note: reserved exclusively for safety_trigger_fired — §E7.3, and §E3.4 audits it as a usage grep. `holdSteps` is two seconds on the 12 fps clock: long enough to be seen, short enough that the deterministic fail-safe does not become ambient lighting.

render.$note: How the frame leaves the renderer, before the press reads it — Phase 19's ship line: "correct colour management (SRGBColorSpace), ACES Filmic tone mapping". Both were specified and neither was set, and the symptom was not a colour cast: linear scene values reached §E6's separation unmapped, so on the story run — brown + sunflower + aqua, with no black plate (§E9.2) — every clay mid-tone solved to full coverage on one plate and the film printed as a flat brown wash with the model invisible in it. Tone mapping is what puts a scene inside an ink's range; these two numbers are that, authored rather than hard-coded because an exposure is an art-direction decision and belongs where the rest of them are.
render.exposureNote: A film exposure, and it is not yet the answer to the story run's flat print — see docs/reports/story-press-flat.md. Raising it from 1.0 to 3.0 and back was measured against the print and moved the sheet's overall lightness without recovering the model, because the density the separation asks for saturates on the one plate that carries the clay whatever the exposure. Held at 1.35 — a modest lift that is defensible on its own terms — until that decision is taken.

story.$note: §E16's film, as the two numbers that decide how much of a reader's scrolling it costs. The acts' shares of the spine are the blueprint's own table and live in src/story/acts.ts; these are how those shares become height.
story.viewportsNote: The reel's total height, in screens. It was 20, which was arithmetic rather than a decision: the cold open is five per cent of the spine, one screen was the floor for a snap point, and 1 / 0.05 = 20. That made the shortest act set the length of the whole film — nine acts over twenty screens, most of them a single paragraph held in the middle of three empty ones. Ten screens keeps every act legible, keeps scroll and `t` linear in each other, and halves what a reader has to spend to reach the receipts. The panels are sticky now, so an act shorter than a screen still holds its copy on screen for the whole act rather than flashing past.
story.panelTopNote: Where an act's copy sits while its act plays, as a share of the viewport. Above centre: the clay is the subject and the type is the caption, and a caption that sits dead centre competes with what it is captioning.
story.scrimReachNote: How far across the frame the reading ground carries before the model is untouched, as a percentage of the stage. The acts set their copy in paper inks — text-secondary is #674f3c, chosen against paper-50 — and on the film those inks were printed straight onto the clay render, where the secondary ones fall to roughly 1.5:1 and the ghost flags and the described lines stopped being readable at all. This is the title-safe answer and it is also the press's own: paper is the ground and the clay is printed on it, so the model emerging out of the sheet at the inline-start edge is §E5's three-material law rather than a veil laid over it to rescue a contrast failure. Fifty-eight per cent is where the copy's measure ends and the figure begins; past it the render is at full strength.

world.$note: The clay city, in metres. The projection is Web Mercator → local ENU metres (M8.2), so every number below is a real ground measurement rather than a scene unit — which is what lets a building height and an SLA radius be argued about in the same units.

kit.note: the kit is generated, not modelled. A 68 m block with 9 m carriageways is the coarse grain of a ward laid out on a grid, and it is honest scenery — it carries no data and is never read as though it did.

pin.note: §E27: a pin's height is severity, not decoration. Six steps is half a second on the 12 fps clock — the Settle motion (§E11.1), which is a pin being pushed into clay rather than a marker fading in.

camera.note: a long lens low over a table. The damping is per second and frame-rate independent, because §E7.2's camera is the one thing in the world that is not stepped.

extent.note: the half-extent of the local ENU frame. Beyond this the Mercator scale correction at the origin latitude stops being a good approximation, and the honest move is a new origin rather than a wider frame.

weather.$note: §E7.4, where the art and the fairness mechanism are the same fact rendered twice. Nothing here decides *whether* it is raining — that comes from the SLA engine's own seasonal adjustment (see clay/sun.ts). These are only the numbers that turn a deadline multiplier into a material property and a solar altitude into a key light, and they live here so the art direction can be tuned without anybody editing the fairness mechanism to do it.
weather.note: soakedMultiplier is the SLA multiplier at which the clay is fully wet: a season that costs a contractor half again as long is a season that has soaked the city, and a tenant who configures 3.0 gets soaked clay rather than a number that keeps climbing off the end of a shading term. monsoonWetness is only the threshold between the two published words for the caption; the material sees the continuous value. twilightDeg is civil twilight rather than the horizon, because a city fifteen minutes after sunset is not black. keyFloor is what is left of the key light at night — the moon, the sodium, the fact that a screen showing nothing is a screen nobody can use. minSunUp holds the sun at the horizon rather than below it, which is a stated deviation: a light source under the ground is not night, it is a lighting bug that looks like a style.

budget.$note: §E23, as numbers the code and the CI assertion both read. A budget written in a table and re-typed in a test is two budgets.
budget.note: vramMb and fps are §E23 verbatim and pins is the gate's stated load. drawCalls is this repository's own number and is tight on purpose: pins are one call, buildings are one call, and the rest is ground, roads, water and the post chain. liteMemoryGb and liteFps are §E13's Tier B triggers — thresholds rather than budgets, but they belong beside them or they get re-typed. degradeBelowFraction and recoverAboveFraction exist because a vsynced display never actually measures 60.00: a healthy frame loop reports 59.4, and a manager that degraded on "below 60" would walk itself to the bottom of the ladder on a machine that was meeting its budget. recoverWindows is the hysteresis, expressed as time rather than as a second frame-rate number — climbing back up takes four consecutive healthy windows, so a scene cannot oscillate across a threshold it is sitting on.
